finding.claim: The unvalidated icon URL supplied to update() is fetched server-side with a GET by the nightly sync() job, enabling blind SSRF to internal or link-local targets.
finding.source: icon parameter of Profile.update(String webhook, String icon) at src/Profile.java:11, reachable via PUT /profile per the comment at line 10 (the handler is not in this repo)

trace.note: update(webhook, icon) accepts icon from the caller
this.iconUrl = icon; stored with no validation
sync(HttpClient c) runs in the nightly job
Server issues a GET to that URI and reads the full body into memory

finding.guards_checked: Regex check at src/Profile.java:12 applies only to webhook, not icon. No scheme, host, IP-range, or port allowlist anywhere in the file. No null check (null causes NPE, not a security control). Redirect policy not set here; HttpClient is injected, so following redirects depends on the caller's client configuration and must be verified at construction. Response body is discarded, so the request is blind; impact is internal reachability, status/timing-based port probing, and GET side effects.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is the regex at src/Profile.java:12, which applies to webhook and not icon. Nothing validates icon at lines 16, 20-24, or elsewhere in the file. The HttpClient is injected, so redirect policy is not visible here, but the initial GET to the attacker-supplied URI at line 23-24 happens regardless of redirects.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches: icon is stored unvalidated at src/Profile.java:16, and sync() at lines 23-24 issues a server-side GET to URI.create(iconUrl) with no scheme, host, or IP check. The source is the PUT /profile body per the comment at line 10, which a user can set for their own profile. The handler is not in the repo, so its auth requirements are unverified, but any authenticated low-privilege user would still be an attacker here.
